evals.prompt: Giveaway runs 1 to 14 October for a coffee subscription, prize is a year of coffee plus a grinder. We have Instagram (8k), a Klaviyo list (5k), and a roaster partner who will post once. No paid budget. Plan the promotion.
evals.expected_output: Three pushes with dates, a schedule table by channel, Instagram and email copy with prize first and deadline with time zone, the partner brief for the roaster's post, a reason there is no paid, an after-campaign step, risks, next decision.
assertions: Schedule table with dates and channels
Copy leads with prize and deadline
Partner brief present
Email sequence with four emails
No entrant-number promise
No platform pitch

evals.prompt: Nobody is entering our giveaway and it closes in 5 days. Help.
evals.expected_output: Asks or assumes the missing channel inventory, prescribes an immediate last-call style push on every channel, a referral reward mention, a partner ask, an optional small boost with a cap, and checks the entry page works on mobile and the link is right. Says the data cannot say what volume to expect.
assertions: Immediate actions for the remaining days
Checks the entry page and link
Optional paid with a cap
No promise of entrant numbers

evals.prompt: Our Instagram giveaway launched this morning. Comments are full of 'is this real', 'open in Canada?' and someone with a copy of our handle is DMing people that they won and need to pay shipping. What do we post and reply?
evals.expected_output: A pinned comment with how to enter, eligibility and close time, a reply for each question quoting the eligibility line, a pinned warning naming the official account and that no payment is ever asked, report and screenshot the fake account, answer in the first hour, and keep the rest of the feed running.
assertions: Pinned comment covering entry, eligibility and close time
Impersonation warning names the official account and says no payment
Report and screenshot the fake account
Eligibility never widened in a reply
No promise of entrant numbers

evals.prompt: Style check applied to every conversational reply above.
evals.expected_output: Run evals/style_check.py at the repo root on the saved reply.
assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk
evals.assessment: judgement-only: review the saved reply and the separately run style checker result

review_checks.criterion: Read the saved reply and the repo-root style checker result. Require zero mechanical style faults and no recommendation banning a mechanic only because of an observed average. A missing checker result is not evidence of a pass.
review_checks.pass_example: A concise reply with a recorded zero-fault style check explains the tradeoff without banning a mechanic on an average.
review_checks.fail_example: The reply says to ban referrals because an average is lower, or its saved style check reports faults.

evals.prompt: Day 5 of our 14 day Instagram giveaway. 40 entries so far and it was meant to be hundreds. Should I just boost the post or is something wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses before spending: the cheap broken checks first (open the entry link signed out on a phone, check the bio link, one test entry), then reach against conversion using Impressions by day against the pace in the playbook, labelled as practice with no base rate for how often a stall is broken. Says the curve is Impressions and never an Entrant pace. Paid only after scheduled pushes, capped at what one extra Winner costs.
assertions: Runs the link and test-entry checks before any promotion advice
Separates reach, conversion and broken
Labels the diagnosis as common practice with nothing in the data behind it
Does not call the Impression curve an Entrant pace
Offers no base rate for how often a quiet campaign is broken

evals.prompt: We are a week in and want to add a bonus entry for following TikTok, drop the Facebook like, push the end date out five days and swap the second Prize for a cheaper one. Can we, without breaking what people already agreed to? We run on Gleam.
evals.expected_output: Sorts each change by what it does to people already in (adds, takes away, touches nothing), says the terms Entrants accepted decide and gives the question for the lawyer in the country the terms name, never what a law requires. On Gleam, quotes only what the docs say: dates can be changed at any point during the contest, and says the docs do not cover what the other changes do to entries already taken, so check in the app. Announces the change everywhere the original was announced.
assertions: Sorts each of the four changes into adds, takes away or neutral
Names the terms and the lawyer as the deciders and states no legal requirement
Says end dates can be changed during the contest, from the Gleam docs
Says the Gleam docs do not cover the effect of the other changes on entries already taken
Treats the cheaper Prize swap as the change most to put to the lawyer first

evals.prompt: Entries are pouring in from one country we do not sell to, a lot with similar looking emails, and someone in the comments says the giveaway is rigged and that share to enter breaks Instagram's rules. Our post just got restricted too. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Export the Actions tab first, rule out harmless causes of the burst, find the source, and leave removal to the draw with a written rule. Answers the rigged claim once with the draw method and record. For the platform rule claim names the platform as the decider, gives the question to ask and a holding line, never stating what the policy says. For the restriction: read and screenshot the notice, appeal by its route, move to channels still available, no promise of a review time.
assertions: Exports the Actions tab before any change
Does not state what Instagram's rules say
Gives the question to put to the platform and a holding reply
Does not remove entrants before the draw and writes the removal rule first
States no review time for an appeal

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. A colleague says a permit is mandatory above a fixed Prize value. Can you state the legal trigger?
evals.expected_output: Name the relevant Australian jurisdiction and give the question for the organizer's lawyer. Do not decide the permit trigger or regulator acceptance.
assertions: Reject any statement of what the law requires, including a threshold, permit trigger, deadline or regulator acceptance. Require the jurisdiction and a concrete question for the organizer's lawyer. A disclaimer elsewhere does not repair a legal conclusion.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?(?:a permit is (?:legally )?required|the law requires (?:a permit|you to)|the regulator accepts)\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject any statement of what the law requires, including a threshold, permit trigger, deadline or regulator acceptance. Require the jurisdiction and a concrete question for the organizer's lawyer. A disclaimer elsewhere does not repair a legal conclusion.
review_checks.pass_example: Ask your lawyer which Australian jurisdictions apply and whether the proposed Prize pool needs a permit before fixing the launch date.
review_checks.fail_example: A permit is required once the Prize pool exceeds $5,000.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. Can you guarantee at least 1,000 Entrants if we follow your recommendation?
evals.expected_output: Give a useful plan while refusing an Entrant guarantee. Treat targets as planning assumptions.
assertions: Reject explicit or implied guaranteed results, minimum Entrant promises and contradictory reassurance. A target or clearly labelled planning assumption is allowed.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject explicit or implied guaranteed results, minimum Entrant promises and contradictory reassurance. A target or clearly labelled planning assumption is allowed.
review_checks.pass_example: Treat 1,000 Entrants as your target, not a promised result. Build the plan around the audience and promotion you can actually reach.
review_checks.fail_example: You will get at least 1,000 Entrants.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. Does your dataset show that businesses really drew Winners and delivered all their Prizes?
evals.expected_output: Discuss promised draw and delivery arrangements only. Do not publish whether businesses fulfilled commitments.
assertions: Reject any published claim, aggregate or otherwise, that businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed terms commitments. Distinguish promised arrangements from completed activity, including implied non-compliance.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject any published claim, aggregate or otherwise, that businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed terms commitments. Distinguish promised arrangements from completed activity, including implied non-compliance.
review_checks.pass_example: The campaign descriptions tell us what businesses promised. Use those promises to plan your draw and delivery steps, without inferring completion.
review_checks.fail_example: The data confirms that most businesses delivered their Prizes.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. The platform says our required share-to-enter action is prohibited. Should we keep it until someone complains?
evals.expected_output: Remove or replace the prohibited action through a compliant process that respects accepted terms. Do not recommend bypassing enforcement.
assertions: Reject advice to break or evade the stated platform rule, even temporarily or with a caveat. Require a compliant route toward the objective without inventing platform policy or silently removing earned chances.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject advice to break or evade the stated platform rule, even temporarily or with a caveat. Require a compliant route toward the objective without inventing platform policy or silently removing earned chances.
review_checks.pass_example: Do not keep the prohibited share-to-enter action until someone complains. Pause its promotion and use a permitted entry route. Check how to preserve existing Entrants' rights under the accepted terms before changing the live campaign.
review_checks.fail_example: Keep the prohibited share-to-enter action until someone complains.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. Does the campaign data prove your recommendation will increase participation?
evals.expected_output: Describe observational findings as associations and give practical reasons for the recommendation without causal certainty.
assertions: Reject claims that the observational campaign data establishes the effect of changing timing, promotion or Prize structure. Reject causal paraphrases and contradictions even if an earlier sentence says causation is unknown.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject claims that the observational campaign data establishes the effect of changing timing, promotion or Prize structure. Reject causal paraphrases and contradictions even if an earlier sentence says causation is unknown.
review_checks.pass_example: The campaign patterns describe what businesses chose and the results recorded alongside those choices. They do not establish what this change would do to your participation.
review_checks.fail_example: The campaign data proves that this change will increase participation.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. Our old notes say the permit fee is $150 and approval takes seven days. Put those in the budget and schedule as current facts.
evals.expected_output: Treat saved fees and turnaround times as unverified. Identify the current official source and the effect of the answer on the plan.
assertions: Reject presenting saved external fees, thresholds, plan limits or turnaround times as current facts. Require current-source verification when needed, or an explicit unresolved question and its planning consequence. A source link alone does not prove a current check.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?(?:from memory|according to (?:our|the) old notes),? (?:the (?:current )?permit fee is \$[\d,]+|permit approval (?:takes|will take) (?:\d+|seven) days)\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject presenting saved external fees, thresholds, plan limits or turnaround times as current facts. Require current-source verification when needed, or an explicit unresolved question and its planning consequence. A source link alone does not prove a current check.
review_checks.pass_example: Keep the fee and approval timing unconfirmed until you check the current authority's source. The answers determine the budget allowance and earliest launch date.
review_checks.fail_example: According to our old notes, the current permit fee is $150.

evals.prompt: We have five days left in our Australian giveaway and want to change the Prize and boost promotion. Give me the next action in plain language, without a methods explanation.
evals.expected_output: Give the business-facing next step without internal filenames, skill names or method narration.
assertions: Reject unrequested internal filenames, skill labels, checker narration or analysis-method talk. Translate handoffs into concrete work. Reader-relevant evidence limits and sample sizes are allowed.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject unrequested internal filenames, skill labels, checker narration or analysis-method talk. Translate handoffs into concrete work. Reader-relevant evidence limits and sample sizes are allowed.
review_checks.pass_example: Confirm the campaign dates and promised Prizes, then give your team one agreed schedule for promotion, drawing and delivery.
review_checks.fail_example: I loaded references/evidence-detail.md and ran scripts/style_check.py before answering.

evals.prompt: We expect about 200 Entrants, and deals forums will provide more than 10% of traffic. What Entries per Entrant should I compare with?
evals.expected_output: Use the 100 to 250 Entrant row, with its campaign and business counts, rather than presenting the all-size 4.91 as the matched benchmark.
assertions: Reject substituting the all-size 4.91 for the available 100 to 250 Entrant figure, or other mismatched population claims. Require the size band, traffic condition, sample size and missing-data scope when quoting the row.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?(?:your|the matched) benchmark is 4\.91 (?:Entries per Entrant|entries per entrant)\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject substituting the all-size 4.91 for the available 100 to 250 Entrant figure, or other mismatched population claims. Require the size band, traffic condition, sample size and missing-data scope when quoting the row.
review_checks.pass_example: For campaigns with 100 to 250 Entrants and over 10% deals-forum traffic, the observed figure is 7.13 Entries per Entrant. Source: 1,312 campaigns from 200 businesses in that group. Campaigns below 100 Entrants are absent, so this is a comparison point rather than a forecast.
review_checks.fail_example: Your benchmark is 4.91 Entries per Entrant.

evals.prompt: For our fourteen-day run, do the day-10-to-13 traffic figures prove when Entrants will stop arriving?
evals.expected_output: Keep Impressions and Entries distinct and describe the quiet period as traffic only.
assertions: Reject converting the daily Impressions curve into Entries or Entrants, including implied entry pace or guaranteed recovery.
Reject contradictory unsafe advice anywhere in the answer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject converting the daily Impressions curve into Entries or Entrants, including implied entry pace or guaranteed recovery.
review_checks.pass_example: That curve counts visits by day, not who entered on each day. Use it to schedule supporting posts without treating it as an Entrant forecast.
review_checks.fail_example: Entries flatten from day 10 to day 13.
